articles.summary: Productivity platform Todoist has confirmed a cyberattack that resulted in the theft of data belonging to 6% of its customer base. The compromised information includes user email addresses, hashed passwords, and account creation dates.

articles.title: Fed’s preferred inflation gauge lands with a December rate increase already priced in

Investors had largely anticipated a December interest rate hike before the report was issued, suggesting that the new figures will not significantly alter current economic projections.

articles.title: As food prices rise, do shoppers still care about sustainability?
articles.summary: Rising grocery costs are prompting many consumers to weigh their environmental values against the constraints of a tighter budget. While interest in eco-friendly products remains significant, inflation is leading some shoppers to prioritize lower prices over sustainable certifications. This shift indicates that economic pressure is increasingly influencing the balance between ethical consumption and financial necessity.

articles.title: We are living in perilous times if Nvidia’s Jensen Huang dictates your 401(k) balance

articles.title: Common sleep and anxiety drugs could be harming aging brains
articles.summary: Research indicates that approximately one-third of older adults with cognitive impairments are using medications that can negatively impact brain function and lead to higher rates of hospitalization. Experts warn that these substances contribute to premature mortality, representing a significant but avoidable risk to the health of the aging population.

articles.title: The ‘drill, baby, drill’ Democrat who will soon help oversee Texas’ oil industry

articles.title: Voters are fed up with for-profit utilities, but they keep rejecting ‘public power’
articles.summary: Despite widespread frustration with the costs and services of private utility companies, voters have repeatedly turned down ballot measures to transition to publicly owned systems. articles.title: A 66-year-old nurse is facing down retirement with just $500 saved. Who’s to blame?
articles.summary: A 66-year-old nurse is nearing the end of her career with only $500 in total savings, highlighting the difficulties many face when approaching their later years. Her situation illustrates the reality that retirement is determined by financial stability rather than simply reaching a specific age. The case underscores the growing trend of older workers who are unable to stop working due to a lack of retirement funds.

articles.title: Scientists discover a new type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat
articles.summary: A newly identified subtype called "circadian depression" may affect nearly 25% of individuals suffering from severe or persistent depressive symptoms. Linked to disruptions in the body's internal clock, this condition is characterized by extreme exhaustion and irregular sleep patterns. Because standard medications often prove ineffective for this group, the discovery provides a potential explanation for treatment resistance in many patients.

articles.title: Experts warn: Nearly everyone in AI is susceptible to a honey-trap scheme right now
articles.summary: Cybersecurity experts are cautioning that professionals in the artificial intelligence sector are increasingly being targeted by social engineering schemes known as honey-traps. These tactics leverage personal or romantic lures to manipulate individuals into compromising sensitive information or systems. As the industry expands, specialists emphasize the need for tech workers to remain vigilant against these unconventional security threats.
